   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

country.comment: Explicitly studies Brazil from the colonial period to contemporary national census and health data.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1 (Title and Abstract); PDF pp. 11–14 (Figures 1–2)

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative findings are descriptive race-stratified national proportions and counts without inferential statistical testing; the author attributes these disparities to historical-colonial institutional/environmental racism, non-enforcement of constitutional and statutory sanitation/equity mandates, exclusionary urban planning, and omission of racial criteria in policy allocation.
effect_estimate.value: In the 2010 IBGE Census (where Brazil's population was 51% Black and 48% white), Black people represented 61% of the population without water supply access (21,532,754 Black people vs 37% white), 67% without waste collection (17,955,295 Black people vs 30% white), 58% without sewage treatment (48,572,734 Black people vs 40% white), and 76% without a home bathroom (10,610,966 Black people vs 20% white). In DataSUS (1996–2014; N = 231,087 DRSAI deaths, 23% missing race), among the 77% of deaths with race recorded, 55% were Black (97,897 Black deaths, or 1 death every 1.5 hours) vs 43% white (21,270 excess deaths), alongside almost 2 million Black hospitalizations for sanitation-related diseases (Jan 2008–Oct 2016); no regression models, CIs, or p-values are reported.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1 (Abstract); PDF pp. 11–15 (Figures 1–2 and text)

mechanism_certainty.comment: Empirical tabulations measure only demographic disparities by race/color in sanitation inadequacy and DRSAI mortality/hospitalization; no legal, administrative, planning, or enforcement variable is empirically measured or directly observed, so the causal role of specific institutional/legal mechanisms (non-enforcement of Law 11.445/2007 and PNSIPN, exclusionary urban planning, exclusion from participatory spaces) is inferred from secondary literature and historical-political reasoning.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 3 (Introduction); PDF pp. 11–18 (Results and Final considerations)

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines non-enforcement/non-implementation of constitutional and statutory rights to universal and prioritized basic sanitation (1988 Constitution arts. 196, 200, 225; Law 11.445/2007; Law 12.288/2010; PNSIPN 2013), marginalization of Black spaces (favelas, peripheries, quilombola/ribeirinho communities) in urban/environmental planning and policy prioritization criteria, and exclusion of Black populations and social movements from participatory/deliberative policy spaces.
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 3 (Introduction); PDF p. 7; PDF p. 11; PDF pp. 15–18 (Final considerations)

outcome_flags.comment: Directly analyzes race-disaggregated lack of water supply access, lack of sewage treatment/disposal and home bathrooms, and overall basic sanitation service coverage deficits (including solid waste collection) in the 2010 IBGE Census.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 3 (Introduction); PDF pp. 11–12 (Figure 1 and text)

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Study is a political-historical and legal-institutional analysis (examining colonial legacies, the 1988 Constitution, Basic Sanitation Law 11.445/2007, Statute of Racial Equality Law 12.288/2010, and PNSIPN 2013) supplemented by descriptive national census/mortality tabulations rather than an analytical cross-sectional regression/survey study, primary qualitative fieldwork, or systematic review.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 1 (Abstract); PDF p. 3 (Introduction); PDF p. 5 (Introduction); PDF pp. 11–18

sample_size.comment: Combines exploratory bibliographic review with descriptive national secondary statistics from the 2010 IBGE Census (exact total national population denominator not printed in text) and national DataSUS mortality (1996–2014) and hospitalization (2008–2016) registries.
sample_size.value: National population data from IBGE 2010 Census (total N not reported; includes up to 48,572,734 Black individuals with inadequate sewage disposal, 21,532,754 without water supply network access, 17,955,295 without waste collection, and 10,610,966 without a bathroom); 231,087 deaths from diseases related to inadequate environmental sanitation (DRSAI) in DataSUS/SIM (1996–2014); almost 2 million hospitalizations of Black individuals in DataSUS (January 2008–October 2016)

study_design.comment: Author describes the design as exploratory-level bibliographic research (citing Gil, 2009) from a political-historical perspective paired with descriptive race-stratified analysis of 2010 IBGE Census sanitation data and 1996–2016 Tabnet DataSUS morbidity/mortality records.
study_design.value: Exploratory bibliographic and political-historical institutional analysis combined with descriptive secondary analysis of national census (IBGE 2010) and administrative health (DataSUS 1996–2016) data
